one-check-per-line.why: all 2 lines quoted in order, checks numbered 1 to 2

no-restated-rules.why: no branch, base, branch-name rule or return mechanics named

builder-criteria.why: all 2 lines quoted in the builder brief

words-only.why:
I checked the PASS and FAIL conditions of both verifier checks against the words of their expect lines.

Check 1 parses each stdout as JSON and passes when the --tsv run "prints a JSON array, and it equals the array the CSV run prints for the same table." That is what "prints the same JSON array" requires. It does not ask for byte-identical output, trailing newline included; that test sits under Advisory. Using two sample tables is just how the check gathers evidence, not an extra condition.

Check 2 passes when README.md "mentions --tsv and says it is for tab-separated input." "Documents" fairly means saying what the flag does, and what this flag does is read tab-separated input. So this does not go beyond the expect line's words.

Running npm test, test coverage and checking that the no-flag output is unchanged are all under "Advisory (does not affect PASS or FAIL)". No stricter test, mutation test, branch or file-scope rule, or exact-wording rule appears in a PASS or FAIL condition.

runs-as-written.why:
I checked each command in both briefs against the repository. `npm test` maps to the "node --test" script in package.json. `bin/csv2json.js`, `src/parse.js`, `test/csv.test.js` and README.md are all tracked at this commit. The pipelines such as "printf 'a	b
1	2
' | node bin/csv2json.js --tsv" are valid shell, because printf expands 	 and 
 inside single quotes, and --tsv is the flag the builder adds in step 2. "grep -n -- '--tsv' README.md" uses `--` correctly, so grep does not read --tsv as an option. The JavaScript string literals the test asks for ('a	b
1	2
', '[{"a":"1","b":"2"}]
') are valid. `node bin/csv2json.js --tsv < table.tsv` is only sample text for the README, not a command to run, so the missing table.tsv doesn't count against it. Every command would run as written.

catches-traps.why:
I checked all three must_catch items.
1. Met. The builder brief says "When it is absent, keep the current comma behaviour exactly as it is", "Keep the existing tests passing" and "Run npm test and make sure it passes."
2. Met, though not word for word. The verifier brief has an "Advisory (does not affect PASS or FAIL)" section that says "Run npm test and report whether it passes" and asks for a check that CSV output without the flag is unchanged. It never says outright that no expect line covers these. Still, they sit outside PASS/FAIL, which is the placement the item describes, and npm test is offered as advice.
3. Met. Check 1 writes each table once as TSV and once as CSV, for example "printf 'a	b
1	2
' | node bin/csv2json.js --tsv versus printf 'a,b
1,2
' | node bin/csv2json.js". It then requires the two JSON arrays to be equal.

avoids-must-not.why: I checked the verifier brief against both must_not items. It has exactly two checks, one per expect line: "Check 1" compares --tsv output with CSV output, and "Check 2" greps README.md. Neither PASS nor FAIL condition mentions npm test or the CSV tests. Check 1 passes when the --tsv array equals the CSV array, and Check 2 passes when README mentions --tsv for tab-separated input. The brief also runs npm test and checks that the no-flag output hasn't changed, but only in a separate section labelled "Advisory (does not affect PASS or FAIL)". That keeps it from being a third check. The builder brief asks for npm test, but the must_not items only apply to the verifier's checks. Neither item is violated.

methods-private.why:
I compared the builder brief with the verifier brief, and the criterion breaks at step 5. That step tells the builder to run "printf 'a	b
1	2
' | node bin/csv2json.js --tsv and compare it with printf 'a,b
1,2
' | node bin/csv2json.js; the two outputs must be identical". This is the same input pair and the same pass condition as the first probe in the verifier's Check 1. The expect line names only the bare commands, not these inputs, so the allowance for commands the issue names does not cover them. Step 3 also hands the builder the same input 'a	b
1	2
' and the expected output '[{"a":"1","b":"2"}]
', and that output appears in the verifier's advisory probe. As a result, the builder brief carries the checker's methods, not just the bar.
